why: Every critical kernel mutation is classified. `detected` must redden at least one test; `equivalent` and `excepted` must keep the suite green and say why. The gate fails closed on a mutation that cannot be applied, because a replacement that matches nothing would otherwise pass by doing nothing. See scripts/check_mutations.py and docs/swe-standalone/14-mutation-gate.md. A detected mutation must also name the tests it reddens (expected_red); a non-zero exit from a build error or an unrelated test does not count as detection.
